title: Formalize Ellis-Friedgut-Pilpel EKR theorem for permutations

problemStatement.plain: Formalize the permutation analogue of the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem: a family of permutations in which any two permutations agree on at least one point has size at most (n-1)!.
whyMatters: This is the Ellis-Friedgut-Pilpel extension of EKR from set systems to permutations.
It connects extremal combinatorics with symmetric group actions, derangement graphs, spectral graph theory, and representation theory.

proven: Ellis-Friedgut-Pilpel (2011) prove the mathematical theorem that a 1-intersecting family in S_n has size at most (n-1)!.
The related gallery proof erdos-ko-rado already formalizes parent EKR infrastructure such as intersecting families and star families, with Katona's cyclic permutation argument axiomatized.

# Knowledge Base: erdos-ko-rado-oq-04

## Problem Understanding

The selected target is the Ellis-Friedgut-Pilpel permutation analogue of the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem. In plain terms, if a family of permutations of `n` points has the property that any two permutations agree somewhere, then the family has size at most `(n - 1)!`.

## Current Evidence

- `selection-report.md` identifies this as a first-time exploration with EMPTY prior knowledge.
- `state.md` keeps the problem in OBSERVE with zero attempts.
- The parent gallery proof `erdos-ko-rado` is relevant but does not by itself prove the permutation theorem.

## Possible Routes

1. Define the derangement graph on `S_n` and prove the bound via an eigenvalue or representation-theoretic independence-number argument.
2. Investigate whether a junta/combinatorial reformulation gives a more formalization-friendly path.
3. If the full proof is too large, state the theorem with explicit axiomatic assumptions, following the parent EKR proof's scoped-axiom pattern.

## Dead Ends

No approaches have been tried yet.
